shifts.summary: The first shift was overall moderate in difficulty. Candidates reported attempting between 72 and 80 questions successfully. Reasoning was generally easy with 17–24 good attempts, while General Awareness showed a mixed difficulty and 15–17 good attempts. Quantitative section difficulty varied, with 14–22 good attempts. English difficulty ranged from easy to moderate with 17 good attempts.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Reasoning was the longest part, many statement‑based items. Candidates felt attempts were low.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: GA content included current affairs up to 2023 and a few recent items. Scope was limited but questions were straightforward for some.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Math featured advanced problems and some lengthy items, causing time pressure.

topics.topic: Number of frames in a standard ten‑pin bowling game
Volume of a prism – base area calculation

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: English had many passage‑based items and a focus on direct/indirect speech and voice transformation.

observations: Rain reduced attendance to 8 of 24 students.
Computer seat change and system lag caused distractions and delays.
Timing shortage was noted, especially in the Math section.
Candidates reported overall attempts between 69 and 80 questions.
disagreements: GA difficulty was reported as Easy by one source and Difficult by another, leading to a range Easy to Moderate.
Quant difficulty was described as Easy, Moderate, and Difficult across different reports.

intro: On 12 October 2026, the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam was conducted in three shifts. The first shift was reported as moderate in difficulty with unofficial figures indicating 72–80 good attempts overall. The second shift showed a range from easy to moderate, but the number of good attempts was not reliably reported. The third shift remains pending, as no usable analysis has been published yet. All figures are unofficial and SSC normalises scores across shifts.
